title: A Giant Storm Soaks the Northeast — and Even a Wedding Gets Washed Out
summary:
Imagine a storm that just... won't... leave. That's what's happening in the northeast U.S. right now. A slow-moving nor'easter (a big storm that comes up the coast) is bringing high winds, heavy rain, and huge waves to the mid-Atlantic and New England.

About 100,000 customers lost electricity on Saturday. Tens of millions of people are in the storm's path. "There will be a lot of high winds, a lot of high tides and heavy rain possibility over the next few days," said Bob Oravec, a lead forecaster with the National Weather Service.

At Surf City Marina on the Jersey Shore, owner Kenny Formica watched water rise inside his building through security cameras. That almost never happens — the last time was Hurricane Sandy, which caused more than $4 million in damage to his business. "This is like an 8,000-pound boat and, you know, a $150,000 boat — just gone," he said.

The storm also changed big plans. Hundreds of flights were cancelled at Boston Logan airport. The Red Sox and Cubs moved their Sunday baseball game all the way to Florida. Singer Ed Sheeran cancelled two concerts. And in North Carolina, a couple's wedding got scrambled when a highway closed and most of their 45 guests were stuck on the other side.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul warned: "Mark my words: Much more is coming."
why_it_matters: Big storms can close airports, roads and schools and cut off electricity, which is why families are told to prepare and stay safe when a huge weather event is on the way.

background_read: A nor'easter is a storm that forms along the U.S. East Coast, usually in fall or winter. Its winds blow in from the northeast, which is how the storm gets its name.
The National Weather Service (the U.S. government office that watches the weather and warns people about dangerous storms) said the wind, rain and high tides would last for days.
Hurricane Sandy (a giant storm that flooded the New York and New Jersey coast in 2012) is the last time the marina owner saw water rise inside his building.
Article_Structure: WHO: A slow-moving nor'easter, tens of millions of people in the mid-Atlantic and New England, and people whose plans changed like Ed Sheeran and a wedding couple
WHAT: The storm brought high winds, heavy rain and huge waves, knocked out power for about 100,000 customers, cancelled flights and shows, and moved a baseball game and a wedding
WHERE: The northeast United States — the mid-Atlantic, New England, the Jersey Shore, Boston Logan airport and North Carolina
WHY: The huge, slow storm is dangerous for people and property, so officials cancelled events and warned that much more is coming

perspectives.description: They worry about flooding and damage — the marina owner watched water rise inside his building and lost expensive boats.
They say the storm is serious, warn about days of high winds and tides, and tell people to get ready for more.
Wedding guests, concert fans and sports teams had plans scrambled, which is disappointing even though it keeps people out of danger.
